answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is binding and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle (ruling out `renew_incumbent`, `negotiate_terms`, and `defer_decision`). Memory c2 indicates the low-cost vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost cut last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—supporting a clean primary switch. Memory c3 shows that dual-sourcing previously removed a single-point-of-failure risk during a constrained-component shortage, which is directly relevant given the assembly line is running at 94% with no buffer. I want to verify c2 to confirm the cost savings and operational smoothness hold under the new quoted price, and c3 to understand whether the second-source pattern can be replicated cheaply in a follow-up cycle once the primary switch is locked in. If c2 confirms the low-cost vendor's reliability and c3 confirms the dual-source playbook, switching primary now satisfies the mandate while preserving a known path to add delivery redundancy next review.
